101.pattern: Node NotReady → ssh → kubelet stopped → enable --now

clues.means: Run this first — every task is on its own host

clues.q: Your fix must survive a reboot of node01
clues.means: systemctl enable (with --now to also start it)

traps: systemctl start only — not enabled after reboot
Skipping ssh cka01001 → you work on the wrong cluster
No sudo -i on node01 in the exam → systemctl says Access denied
Forgetting to exit (root, then node01) before kubectl
memorise: ssh cka01001; k get nodes   # NotReady (wait ~60 s if still Ready)
systemctl enable --now kubelet; systemctl is-enabled kubelet

102.pattern: Service has no endpoints → fix selector to match pod labels

clues.q: does not forward traffic to the Pods

clues.means: Don't relabel pods — change the Service only

traps: Relabelling pods/deployment (forbidden)
If the selector KEY itself is wrong, a merge patch ADDS a second key (selector = AND, still no match); then k edit svc and fix the key instead
Forgetting -n shop

verify.cmd: k -n shop run tmp --rm -it --restart=Never --image=busybox:1.36 -- wget -qO- -T3 cart

memorise: k -n shop get svc cart -o wide   # SELECTOR

103.pattern: Pod Pending → Insufficient memory → set smaller request

clues.q: Set the memory request of the container to 128Mi
Keep the number of replicas unchanged
clues.means: Don't scale down to make it fit

traps: Scaling replicas down instead of fixing requests
Setting --limits instead of --requests
If a memory limit exists, it must be ≥ 128Mi or the spec is invalid
memorise: k -n batch describe pod -l app=reporter | grep -A3 Events
k -n batch set resources deploy reporter --requests=memory=128Mi

104.pattern: Restarts with no app error → wrong livenessProbe port

clues.means: describe pod → Events: Liveness probe failed

clues.q: The nginx container listens on port 80

clues.means: Fix with k edit on the deployment (not the pod)

traps: Changing containerPort instead of the probe port
Removing the probe entirely (changes behaviour, may fail the check)
Editing the pod instead of the deployment
memorise: k -n web describe pod -l app=api | grep -i -A2 liveness
k -n web edit deploy api   # livenessProbe: httpGet: port: 8080 → 80; Esc :wq
k -n web rollout status deploy api; k -n web get pods   # new pod RESTARTS 0

105.pattern: Filter pod logs with grep into a file

clues.q: into the file /opt/course/5/errors.txt on the controlplane node
clues.means: The host you ssh'd into IS this task's controlplane: redirect > there; mkdir -p the folder first (exam: sudo if Permission denied)

traps: Writing the file on the wrong host
Using grep -i (would also catch 'error' lowercase)
Folder missing → 'No such file or directory'
memorise: k -n ops logs legacy-app | grep ERROR > /opt/course/5/errors.txt

106.pattern: helm template + install with same --set (CRDs off)

clues.means: --set crds.install=false (key found with helm show values)
helm install uses the same --version 7.7.3 and --set crds.install=false

traps: Installing without --set crds.install=false → CRD ownership conflict
Forgetting --version 7.7.3 on install
Missing namespace argocd (use --create-namespace if it doesn't exist)

verify.see: Running (may take 2–3 min; Pending for lack of resources is OK in the playground)

memorise: helm repo add argocd https://argoproj.github.io/argo-helm; helm repo update
helm template argocd argocd/argo-cd --version 7.7.3 --namespace argocd --set crds.install=false > /root/argo-helm.yaml
helm install argocd argocd/argo-cd --version 7.7.3 --namespace argocd --set crds.install=false

107.pattern: Prepare node: dpkg -i, enable service, sysctl file

clues.q: Install the Debian package /root/cri-dockerd.deb using dpkg
Enable and start the cri-docker service

clues.means: Write exactly that file, then sysctl --system

traps: sysctl -w (not persistent)
modprobe br_netfilter only → gone after reboot; also write br_netfilter (and nf_conntrack) to /etc/modules-load.d/k8s.conf
Wrong file name — the question names /etc/sysctl.d/k8s.conf
On Killercoda (no Docker) cri-docker fails to START — enable still worked; check is-enabled

verify.cmd: dpkg -l | grep cri-dockerd; systemctl is-enabled cri-docker

memorise: systemctl enable --now cri-docker; systemctl is-enabled cri-docker
cat <<'EOF' > /etc/sysctl.d/k8s.conf   # paste the 4 lines, then EOF

108.pattern: List CRDs / explain a custom field into files

clues.means: k get crd -l app.kubernetes.io/name=cert-manager > /root/resources.yaml (keeps the header)

clues.q: do not set an output format
clues.means: No -o yaml even though the file ends in .yaml

clues.q: subject specification field of the Certificate

traps: Adding -o yaml because of the .yaml file name
Explaining certificate.subject (missing spec)
Listing certificates instead of CRDs

verify.see: NAME / CREATED AT header + 6 cert-manager CRDs

memorise: k get crd -l app.kubernetes.io/name=cert-manager > /root/resources.yaml   # fallback: k get crd | grep cert-manager

109.pattern: ServiceAccount + Role + RoleBinding, imperative, then auth can-i

clues.q: allows only get, list and watch on pods

traps: --serviceaccount=reporter without finance: → kubectl error (must be <namespace>:<name>)
Forgetting -n finance on the rolebinding → it lands in default
Creating a ClusterRole instead of a Role
Spaces in the --verb list

verify.cmd: k -n finance auth can-i list pods --as=system:serviceaccount:finance:reporter
k -n finance auth can-i delete pods --as=system:serviceaccount:finance:reporter
k -n finance auth can-i list secrets --as=system:serviceaccount:finance:reporter

memorise: k -n finance auth can-i watch pods --as=system:serviceaccount:finance:reporter

110.pattern: Named containerPort + NodePort Service targeting the port name

clues.q: add a port specification named http exposing port 80/tcp
clues.means: ports: - name: http containerPort: 80 protocol: TCP on container nginx
nodePort: 30080 in the Service YAML (30000–32767 range)

traps: Service selector not matching pod labels → no endpoints
Leaving out nodePort: 30080 → a random port is chosen
Forgetting name: http on the containerPort, so targetPort: http fails
memorise: cat <<'EOF' | k apply -f -   # Service: type NodePort, selector app: front-end, ports: name http, port 80, targetPort http, nodePort 30080

111.pattern: Ingress → Gateway (HTTPS listener + TLS) + HTTPRoute, delete Ingress

clues.q: with an HTTPS listener on port 443 for hostname gateway.web.example
clues.means: listeners: protocol HTTPS, port 443, hostname gateway.web.example
tls: mode: Terminate, certificateRefs: - kind: Secret name: web-tls

clues.q: sends all paths (/) for gateway.web.example to Service web on port 80
Delete the Ingress web when done

traps: HTTPS listener without a tls block → apply fails with a validation error
parentRefs name typo (must be web-gateway; no namespace needed, same namespace)
Forgetting namespace web-app in metadata

verify.cmd: k -n web-app get gateway web-gateway -o jsonpath='{.spec.listeners}'

memorise: k -n web-app get ingress web -o yaml | grep -A12 '^spec'
vim gw.yaml   # Gateway: gatewayClassName nginx; listener https/HTTPS/443/hostname gateway.web.example; tls: mode Terminate, certificateRefs Secret web-tls
vim route.yaml   # HTTPRoute: parentRefs web-gateway; hostnames gateway.web.example; PathPrefix /; backendRefs web 80
k apply -f gw.yaml -f route.yaml; k -n web-app delete ingress web

112.pattern: Pick the least-permissive NetworkPolicy file and apply it

clues.q: apply the ONE that allows this traffic with the least permissions
clues.means: Read all files; reject ones allowing all pods/namespaces or all ports

clues.q: Do not delete or modify the existing policies
clues.means: Only k apply the chosen file

traps: Choosing a policy with namespaceSelector: {} (all namespaces) or no ports
namespaceSelector and podSelector as SEPARATE '- from' items = OR (too open); in ONE item = AND
Applying more than one file

verify.cmd: k -n frontend exec deploy/frontend -- wget -qO- -T2 backend.backend | head -4

memorise: cat /root/netpol/*.yaml   # narrow namespace+pod selector AND port 80
k -n frontend exec deploy/frontend -- wget -qO- -T2 backend.backend

clues.q: minimum of 1 and a maximum of 4 replicas

traps: behavior under metrics instead of directly under spec
scaleUp instead of scaleDown
Forgetting -n autoscale

verify.cmd: k -n autoscale get hpa apache-server -o jsonpath='{.spec.behavior.scaleDown}'

memorise: vim hpa.yaml   # autoscaling/v2 HPA: scaleTargetRef Deployment apache-server; minReplicas 1; maxReplicas 4; cpu averageUtilization 50

# in hpa.yaml under spec:
spec:
  behavior:
    scaleDown:
      stabilizationWindowSeconds: 30
k apply -f hpa.yaml; k -n autoscale get hpa apache-server

115.pattern: New default StorageClass; un-default all others

clues.q: it must be the ONLY default
clues.means: First patch every old default SC to is-default-class "false", then create local-fast with "true"

traps: Leaving the old default → two (default)
Deleting/recreating the old SC
Unquoted "true" in the annotation
memorise: k patch sc local-path -p '{"metadata":{"annotations":{"storageclass.kubernetes.io/is-default-class":"false"}}}'   # repeat for each old default
docs: 'storage classes' → name local-fast; annotation storageclass.kubernetes.io/is-default-class: "true"; provisioner rancher.io/local-path; volumeBindingMode: WaitForFirstConsumer → k apply

116.pattern: PVC that binds to an existing PV; point deployment at it

clues.means: k get pv mariadb-pv → read class, mode, size

clues.q: so that it binds to the existing PV
clues.means: Match storageClassName ("" if the PV has none) and set volumeName: mariadb-pv

traps: Omitting storageClassName → default SC is used and PVC won't bind to mariadb-pv
PV stuck Released with an old claimRef → k patch pv mariadb-pv -p '{"spec":{"claimRef":null}}'
Forgetting to change claimName in the deploy file
memorise: k get pv mariadb-pv   # Released? → k patch pv mariadb-pv -p '{"spec":{"claimRef":null}}'
PVC YAML: name mariadb, ns mariadb, RWO, 250Mi, storageClassName: "", volumeName: mariadb-pv → k apply
sed -i 's/claimName: ""/claimName: mariadb/' /root/mariadb-deploy.yaml   # replace text in the file
k apply -f /root/mariadb-deploy.yaml; k -n mariadb get pods

201.pattern: Node NotReady → kubelet fails → fix systemd drop-in path

clues.means: Someone edited config: check systemctl cat kubelet

clues.q: why the kubelet does not start on node01
clues.means: ssh node01; systemctl status + journalctl -u kubelet
Fix the unit/drop-in file, not apt

traps: Forgetting systemctl daemon-reload after editing the drop-in
Editing kubelet.service instead of the 10-kubeadm.conf drop-in that holds ExecStart
No sudo -i on node01 in the exam → Permission denied
Reinstalling kubelet (forbidden)
memorise: systemctl status kubelet --no-pager; journalctl -u kubelet --no-pager | tail -5
which kubelet; systemctl cat kubelet | grep ExecStart=   # LAST one wins
systemctl cat kubelet | grep '^# /'   # path of 10-kubeadm.conf
systemctl daemon-reload; systemctl restart kubelet; exit; exit

202.pattern: New pods Pending, no Events → scheduler broken → fix manifest

clues.q: stays Pending, even though nodes have free resources
clues.means: Not a resource issue → scheduler not running

traps: crictl logs is EMPTY when the binary never started — read describe pod (Message) or journalctl -u kubelet
Recreating the pod — it's the scheduler that's broken
Editing the mirror pod with kubectl edit instead of the manifest file
Not waiting ~30 s for kubelet to recreate the static pod

verify.cmd: k -n kube-system get pods | grep scheduler

memorise: k get pod stuck -o wide   # NODE <none>
k -n kube-system get pods | grep scheduler
k -n kube-system describe pod -l component=kube-scheduler | grep -iE 'reason|message'

203.pattern: Names don't resolve → CoreDNS scaled to 0 → scale up

clues.q: can no longer resolve Service names
from Pod dns-test in namespace lookup
clues.means: Test with k -n lookup exec dns-test -- nslookup

clues.q: Save the output of that nslookup to /root/dns.txt

traps: Saving the failed lookup before fixing DNS
Using a new temp pod instead of dns-test
Restarting pods when replicas are 0
Panicking at NXDOMAIN lines — success = Name/Address for kubernetes.default.svc.cluster.local
If replicas are fine, check k -n kube-system get cm coredns (Corefile) and the kube-dns Service endpoints
memorise: k -n kube-system rollout status deploy coredns
k -n lookup exec dns-test -- nslookup kubernetes.default > /root/dns.txt

205.pattern: Pod can't mount a missing ConfigMap volume → create the ConfigMap

clues.means: k get pods → Init:0/1; describe → FailedMount: configmap not found

clues.q: ConfigMap named inventory-config with key ready and value yes

clues.means: Create the missing object; don't edit the init container

traps: Removing the init container (forbidden)
Wrong key/value case (ready=yes)
Creating the ConfigMap in the default namespace

verify.cmd: k -n stock get cm inventory-config -o yaml

memorise: k -n stock describe pod -l app=inventory | tail -5
k -n stock rollout status deploy inventory --timeout=180s   # re-run if it times out

206.pattern: Install Calico from operator + custom-resources; set pod CIDR

clues.q: The Pod CIDR must match the cluster's configured pod subnet
clues.means: Read podSubnet from kubeadm-config, set cidr: in custom-resources.yaml

traps: k apply on tigera-operator.yaml → annotations Too long; use k create
Not CHECKING the cidr in custom-resources.yaml against podSubnet
Applying custom-resources before the operator CRDs exist → k wait --for=condition=Established crd/installations.operator.tigera.io

verify.cmd: k get tigerastatus; k get pods -n calico-system

memorise: k -n kube-system get cm kubeadm-config -o yaml | grep podSubnet   # or: ps aux | grep -o 'cluster-cidr=[0-9][^ ]*'

curl -fsSLO https://raw.githubusercontent.com/projectcalico/calico/v3.29.2/manifests/custom-resources.yaml; sed -i 's#cidr: 192.168.0.0/16#cidr: 10.244.0.0/16#' custom-resources.yaml   # use YOUR podSubnet
k create -f custom-resources.yaml; k get tigerastatus; k get nodes

207.pattern: etcdctl snapshot save with given certs
traps: Mixing up --cert and --cacert
Old etcdctl without ETCDCTL_API=3 → v2 API, snapshot save fails
No sudo -i in the exam → cannot read /etc/kubernetes/pki
Folder /opt/backup missing → mkdir -p first
Using peer.crt instead of server.crt
memorise: etcdctl --write-out=table snapshot status /opt/backup/etcd-snap.db   # deprecation warning is OK

208.pattern: Write a Kustomize overlay (resources, namespace, prefix, replicas)

clues.q: puts all resources in namespace shop-prod
clues.means: namespace: shop-prod (create the namespace if missing)

clues.q: sets the replicas of Deployment shop to 3
clues.means: replicas: - name: shop count: 3 (original name, not prod-shop)

traps: Using name prod-shop in replicas (use the base name shop)
k apply -f instead of -k
Namespace shop-prod doesn't exist → apply fails
memorise:
# /root/shop-kustomize/overlays/prod/kustomization.yaml:
resources:
- ../../base
namespace: shop-prod
namePrefix: prod-
replicas:
- name: shop
  count: 3
k create ns shop-prod --dry-run=client -o yaml | k apply -f -
k apply -k /root/shop-kustomize/overlays/prod; k -n shop-prod get deploy prod-shop
